articles.title: Is AI giving the US economy a case of Dutch disease? From Dutch gas to American chips.
articles.desc: If the argument holds, the AI build-out is a source of upward pressure on bond yields, power prices and wages for scarce technical staff, which would keep financing costs high for sectors outside technology. That fits with this week’s 24-year high in 10-year Treasury yields, which Bloomberg partly a
articles.content: If the argument holds, the AI build-out is a source of upward pressure on bond yields, power prices and wages for scarce technical staff, which would keep financing costs high for sectors outside technology. That fits with this week’s 24-year high in 10-year Treasury yields, which Bloomberg partly attributed to AI-related corporate borrowing. For equities, the thesis implies widening divergence between AI beneficiaries and consumer-facing companies facing squeezed household budgets, a pattern visible in PepsiCo’s North American results. Energy markets are a complicating factor, as Iran-war oil prices are lifting electricity and input costs independently of AI demand. - The Netherlands found gas and watched the rest of its economy wilt; Derek Thompson’s worry is that America has found AI and is running the same experiment. Summary: Writer Derek Thompson (on X @ @DKThomp) argues the AI investment boom may be causing a form of Dutch disease in the US economy He says the build-out is raising the cost of capital, chips, electricity and engineers, outbidding other sectors Thompson also says inflation is eroding household incomes and median wages have been declining for several months Dutch disease refers to the Netherlands’ 1960s gas boom, which lifted the economy overall but hurt non-gas industries The ongoing surge in Treasury yields, partly linked to AI borrowing, and PepsiCo’s weak US volumes are consistent with parts of the argument The analogy has limits: it works through input competition rather than currency, and AI may eventually lift productivity The boom in artificial intelligence investment may be inflicting a modern version of Dutch disease on the US economy, enriching one sector while raising costs for everyone else, according to writer Derek Thompson. In a Substack post, Thompson, a contributing writer at The Atlantic and co-author of the book Abundance, said he worried that the AI build-out was raising the cost of capital, chips, electricity and engineers, leaving every other sector that relies on those inputs to be outbid. At the same time, he argued, the typical American is seeing inflation erode their income, and he said median wages have been declining for several months. The term Dutch disease describes what happened to the Netherlands after the discovery of the vast Groningen natural gas field in 1959. The windfall lifted national income and the currency, but rising prices and a stronger guilder hurt manufacturing and other industries outside the gas sector. The Economist coined the phrase in the 1970s. There is evidence consistent with parts of Thompson’s argument. US 10-year Treasury yields reached a 24-year high this week, and Bloomberg cited a surge in corporate borrowing to finance AI investment as one of the forces behind the bond selloff, alongside heavy government borrowing and elevated energy prices. PepsiCo this week reported falling North American beverage volumes and lowered prices on snacks, a sign of a cautious consumer. The analogy has limits, however. Classic Dutch disease works largely through a stronger currency that undermines exporters, whereas the AI version, as Thompson frames it, operates through competition for scarce inputs. AI could also eventually lift productivity across the wider economy, a benefit a gas discovery never offered. Other forces are at work too, notably energy prices driven higher by the Iran war, which add to electricity costs and inflation independently of AI demand. Whether the diagnosis holds will depend on data still to come. Electricity prices, wage figures and the pace of AI-linked corporate bond issuance are the measures most likely to show whether the boom is crowding out the rest of the economy or eventually lifting it. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.content: Pioneer Acquisition I Corp Enters Into Business Combination Pioneer Acquisition I Corp Enters Into Business Combination Agreement with Green AI Cloud, a Clean Energy Super Compute AI Platform in Europe Green AI Cloud, Inc. (the “Company”), a clean energy super compute AI platform in Europe, is positioned where accelerating AI data center demand meets a scarcity of power-secured capacity. The Company is a pioneer in clean energy compute and its data centers are designed to run on renewable energy (solar, hydro and wind power). Excess heat from its operations can be converted into a heated liquid for industrial product manufacturing or into regional district-heating infrastructure, believed to result in a net-negative CO2 footprint. The proposed business combination values the Company at a pre-money equity value of $300 million. BROOKLYN, N.Y. and STOCKHOLM, Oct. 08, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Green AI Cloud, Inc. (“ ”), an AI infrastructure company focused on designing, building, and operating high-performance AI data centers with a focus on environmental sustainability and data sovereignty, and Pioneer Acquisition I Corp (Nasdaq: ”), a publicly traded special purpose acquisition company, today announced that they have entered into a definitive agreement (the “ ”) that would result in Green AI Cloud becoming a publicly traded company expected to list on the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“ Green AI Cloud, based in Stockholm, Sweden, is building a differentiated digital infrastructure platform for the AI era through a vertically integrated approach to AI-ready data center development. The Company’s approach aims to combine adaptive reuse of existing real estate, sustainable super compute AI using only renewable energy (solar, hydro and wind power), and integrated power infrastructure to support large-scale compute deployments for enterprise AI customers. The Company’s data centers are designed to run on 100% renewable energy. They utilize tailored liquid-cooling systems, waste heat from the AI servers can be recovered into the regional district-heating infrastructure, believed to result in a net-negative carbon footprint. The Company’s platform provides access to top-tier NVIDIA AI hardware accelerators. Enterprise customers can now train Generative Transformer (GPT)-class models on the platform with the promise of equivalent carbon offsets through Green AI Cloud’s uniquely sustainable and “carbon-intelligent” cloud. Currently, Green AI Cloud has operating and development activity in three strategic locations in Sweden. These sites have the potential to support a multi-gigawatt (“ ”) development pipeline over time while enabling environmental redevelopment and community partnership programs in legacy industrial markets and providing a foundation for expansion into additional markets as AI data center demand continues to grow and power availability, site readiness, and speed of deployment become increasingly important. The Company’s current portfolio comprises a mix of live, contracted and planned capacity across several sites. Each site is engineered to meet customer demand for a secure AI compute environment that cannot be met by large co-location data centers. “This Transaction marks an important milestone for Green AI Cloud and we believe it reflects the strength of our strategy to build AI-ready infrastructure where power availability, speed, and execution matter most,” stated Jacob Bostrom, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Green AI Cloud. “We believe the opportunity is being driven not only by rising AI demand, but also by the growing scarcity of power-secured capacity and the need for faster, more flexible deployment models. articles.title: Bigben Interactive finalise la cession de sa filiale Bigben Connected et annonce la prorogation de la procédure de sauvegarde accélérée
articles.desc: Lesquin, 8 octobre 2026, 18h00
articles.content: Bigben Interactive finalise la cession de sa filiale Bigben Bigben Interactive finalise la cession de sa filiale Bigben Connected et annonce la prorogation de la procédure de sauvegarde accélérée Bigben Interactive finalise la cession de sa filiale Bigben Connected annonce la prorogation de la procédure de sauvegarde accélérée la réalisation de la cession de sa filiale Bigben Connected au profit de Modelabs ; et la prorogation pour une durée de deux mois supplémentaires, de sa période de sauvegarde accélérée. Il est préalablement rappelé que, par jugement en date du 17 août 2026, le Tribunal de commerce de Lille Métropole (le « ») a ouvert une procédure de sauvegarde accélérée au bénéfice de la Société dans le cadre de sa restructuration financière (la « Aux termes d'un communiqué de presse en date du 21 juillet 2026, la Société avait annoncé la signature d'un contrat de cession d'actions sous conditions suspensives (le « ») portant sur l'intégralité du capital social et des droits de vote de sa filiale Bigben Connected au profit de la société Modelabs (la « L’ensemble des conditions suspensives ayant pu être levées, la Cession a été définitivement réalisée. Conformément aux stipulations du Contrat de Cession, une partie du prix de la Cession, à hauteur de 35 M€, a été versée par Modelabs à la Société à la date de réalisation de la Cession. Le solde du prix de la Cession fait l'objet d'un crédit vendeur remboursable par Modelabs à la Société sur une durée de cinq (5) ans à compter de la date de réalisation de la Cession selon des échéances semestrielles (le « »). Le montant du Crédit Vendeur a été arrêté entre les parties à la date de réalisation de la Cession à un montant d’environ 13 M€ ; il est précisé que le montant du Crédit Vendeur sera définitivement arrêté à l'issue de la procédure usuelle de vérification, par Modelabs, des comptes de de Bigben Connected, dans les conditions prévues par le Contrat de Cession. Le montant perçu à la date de réalisation de la Cession (35 M€) sera affecté par la Société selon les principes clés de sa restructuration financière tels que présentés dans son communiqué de presse en date du 22 septembre 2026. Cette opération, réalisée dans le cadre de la Procédure de Sauvegarde Accélérée, marque une étape importante de sa restructuration financière. Prorogation de la Procédure de Sauvegarde Accélérée La Société annonce que, par jugement en date du 7 octobre 2026, le Tribunal a prorogé pour une période de deux mois supplémentaires (du 17 octobre 2026 au 17 décembre 2026), la Procédure de Sauvegarde Accélérée et fixé l’audience d’examen du plan de sauvegarde accélérée de la Société au 9 décembre 2026. Sous l'égide des administrateurs judiciaires désignés par le Tribunal de commerce de Lille Métropole, les créanciers et actionnaires de la Société seront appelés à voter, dans le cadre de classes de parties affectées, sur le projet de plan de sauvegarde accélérée, avant que le Tribunal ne statue sur son adoption. Les opérations de restructuration financière seront mises en œuvre à la suite de cette adoption et devraient s'achever d'ici la fin du premier trimestre 2027. La Société informera le marché, en temps utile, des prochaines étapes de sa restructuration financière, et notamment du calendrier détaillé des opérations sur le capital à venir. La Société confirme que les informations susceptibles d'être qualifiées d'informations privilégiées au sens du règlement (UE) n° 596/2014 du 16 avril 2014 sur les abus de marché, et qui ont pu être données à titre confidentiel à ses créanciers financiers et parties prenantes sous accord de confidentialité, dans le cadre de la procédure de conciliation et des négociations relatives à sa restructuration financière, ont été publiées au marché, soit par le passé, soit dans le cadre du présent communiqué, dans le but de rétablir l'égalité d'accès à l'information relative au groupe formé par la Société et ses filiales entre l'ensemble des investisseurs. 31 filiales

articles.title: Bigben Interactive completes the disposal of its subsidiary Bigben Connected and announces the extension of the accelerated safeguard proceedings
articles.desc: Lesquin, 8 October 2026, 6.00 p.m.
articles.content: Bigben Interactive completes the disposal of its subsidiary Bigben Interactive completes the disposal of its subsidiary Bigben Connected and announces the extension of the accelerated safeguard proceedings Bigben Interactive completes the disposal announces the extension of the accelerated safeguard proceedings Lesquin, 8 October 2026 - Bigben Interactive the completion of the disposal of its subsidiary Bigben Connected to Modelabs; and the extension, for a further period of two months of its accelerated safeguard proceedings. It is recalled that, by a judgment dated 17 August 2026, the Commercial Court ( ) opened accelerated safeguard proceedings ( ) for the benefit of the Company in connection with its financial restructuring (the By a press release dated 21 July 2026, the Company announced the signing of a share purchase agreement, subject to conditions precedent (the ), for the entire share capital and voting rights of its subsidiary Bigben Connected, in favour of Modelabs (the All the conditions precedent having been satisfied, the Disposal has been definitively completed. In accordance with the terms of the Share Purchase Agreement, a portion of the disposal price, in an amount of €35m, was paid by Modelabs to the Company on the completion date of the Disposal. The balance of the disposal price is the subject of a vendor loan repayable by Modelabs to the Company over a period of five (5) years from the completion date of the Disposal, in semi-annual instalments (the ). The amount of the Vendor Loan was fixed between the parties, as at the completion date of the Disposal, at approximately €13m; it is specified that the amount of the Vendor Loan will be definitively determined following the customary process for verification by Modelabs of Bigben Connected's closing accounts, under the conditions set out in the Share Purchase Agreement. The amount received on the completion date of the Disposal (€35m) will be applied by the Company in accordance with the key principles of its financial restructuring, as set out in its press release dated 22 September 2026. This transaction, conducted in connection with the Accelerated Safeguard Proceedings, marks a crucial step in the Company's financial restructuring. Extension of the Accelerated Safeguard Proceedings The Company announces that, by a judgment dated 7 October 2026, the Court extended the Accelerated Safeguard Proceedings for a further period of two months (from 17 October 2026 to 17 December 2026) and set the hearing for the examination of the Company's accelerated safeguard plan for 9 December 2026. Under the supervision of the court-appointed administrators ( ) designated by the Commercial Court of Lille Métropole, the creditors and shareholders of the Company will be called upon to vote, within classes of affected parties ( ), on the draft accelerated safeguard plan, before the Court rules on its adoption. The financial restructuring transactions will be implemented following such adoption and are expected to be completed by the end of the first quarter of 2027. The Company will keep the market informed in due course of the next steps of its financial restructuring, including the detailed timetable for the capital transactions to come. The Company confirms that any information that may qualify as inside information within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No. 596/2014 of 16 April 2014 on market abuse, which may have been disclosed on a confidential basis to its financial creditors and stakeholders under a confidentiality agreement in the context of the conciliation proceedings and the negotiations relating to its financial restructuring, has been published to the market, either previously or in this press release, for the purpose of restoring equal access to information relating to the group formed by the Company and its subsidiaries among all investors. 31 filiales et un réseau de distribution dans plus de 100 pays Bigben est un acteur européen de l’édition de jeux vidéo,

articles.desc: With half of young people seriously considering moving abroad for work, TEFL students describe how teaching could help them take their next career step
articles.content: Looking abroad to get ahead: young Britons explore teaching English overseas as UK career opportunities prove elusive There were 1,982 press releases posted in the last 24 hours and 495,630 in the last 365 days. Looking abroad to get ahead: young Britons explore teaching English overseas as UK career opportunities prove elusive With half of young people seriously considering moving abroad for work, TEFL students describe how teaching could help them take their next career step Young people want the chance to put their skills to use. When applications go unanswered or opportunities in their chosen field are scarce, it’s understandable that they start looking further afield.” LONDON, UNITED KINGDOM, October 8, 2026 / / -- Young Britons struggling to find a foothold in the jobs market are exploring teaching English overseas as a way to build experience, develop skills and widen their career options. at the University of Glasgow found that half of UK 16–29-year-olds have seriously considered moving abroad to find work. The nationally representative poll highlights the frustration facing young people trying to get started in their careers. Responses from UK students and graduates of , the UK’s largest provider of TEFL training, offer a personal perspective on those findings. They describe limited graduate opportunities, unanswered applications and uncertainty about their next steps as reasons for exploring Teaching English as a Foreign Language (TEFL). For UK graduate Beth, looking overseas has already led to a new teaching career. After struggling to find stable employment for more than two years, she started teaching English in South Korea this summer. Beth reported applying for more than 80 jobs in a single month without receiving a reply. Teaching abroad had been a longstanding ambition, and completing her TEFL qualification helped her take that next step. “TEFL has, undoubtedly, given me a major confidence boost and positive outlook on my future career prospects,” she said. She also credited her training with helping her confidently answer interview questions about teaching students with no previous English knowledge - practical preparation that helped her secure the role. Andy Healy, Managing Director of The TEFL Org, said: “Young people want the chance to put their skills to use, gain experience and build a career. When applications go unanswered or opportunities in their chosen field are scarce, it’s understandable that they start looking further afield." “Teaching English abroad can offer a practical way to explore a different career while gaining experience of living and working in another country. These responses show how valuable it can be simply to have another option and a clearer sense of what to do next.” For Isobel, uncertainty about finding work after university prompted her to explore teaching. She completed her TEFL qualification alongside her English degree, giving her the confidence to consider a future overseas. “It's made me feel like my future is more open, definitely. I was never planning to move abroad, but it's really reassuring to know that now I can.” The conversation about overseas opportunities comes as Andy Burnham considers options for Britain’s future EU relationship, including possible membership. A future agreement that made it easier to live and work in Europe could widen young people’s choices. However, neither EU membership nor restored freedom of movement has been agreed. “Any future change that makes working overseas more accessible would be welcome. In the meantime, young people need clear information about the opportunities available today, the qualifications employers expect and the requirements for working in their chosen destination." “A TEFL qualification is a fantastic starting point. articles.title: Solidigm is picking Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley to lead a $10 billion U.S. IPO
articles.desc: The flash memory maker could list as soon as 2027 at a valuation of up to $100 billion, according to Bloomberg
articles.content: SK Hynix's Solidigm taps banks for $10 billion U.S. IPO Solidigm is picking Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley to lead a $10 billion U.S. IPO The flash memory maker could list as soon as 2027 at a valuation of up to $100 billion, according to Bloomberg Solidigm, SK Hynix's flash memory unit, has selected as lead underwriters for a planned U.S. initial public offering that could raise roughly $10 billion, according to , and UBS are among the banks brought on for the deal, citing people familiar with the matter who asked not to be named. A listing could take place as soon as 2027 and value Solidigm at as much as $100 billion, according to Bloomberg. The two lead banks are also working with Solidigm to finalize a pre-IPO funding round, Bloomberg reported. The situation remains fluid, with the final roster of banks and other particulars subject to revision. SK Hynix said in a statement that Solidigm is reviewing various options to strengthen its business competitiveness, but that no specific plans have been confirmed. Representatives for declined to comment, and UBS did not respond to requests for comment, according to Bloomberg. Solidigm traces its origins to 2021, when SK Hynix purchased 's NAND flash business and rebranded the operation as Solidigm. Headquartered in Rancho Cordova, California, Solidigm employs more than 2,000 people at sites spanning three continents and has built its identity around furnishing high-density storage for AI data center customers. Its customers include CoreWeave, Vast Data, Technologies, and Tencent Holdings, according to Bloomberg. The planned IPO has drawn scrutiny in South Korea, where parent-subsidiary listings have long been a source of investor concern. According to , critics argue that a separate Solidigm listing could dilute the value already reflected in SK Hynix's share price and harm existing shareholders. Rules that South Korean regulators put in place in August bar most parent-subsidiary listings at home, though the Korea Times noted that the restrictions carry no automatic force when the subsidiary lists abroad. Rep. Ahn Cheol-soo of South Korea's People Power Party called on SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won to clarify whether the IPO will proceed, according to the Korea Times. , the largest U.S. share sale ever by a foreign company, giving American investors direct access to the world's leading producer of high-bandwidth memory chips. Shares in SK Hynix's U.S.-traded depositary receipts dropped 4.3% once the post-listing lockup preventing insiders from selling shares came to an end. articles.title: How Nations Can Turn Their Strengths Into Space Leadership
articles.desc: The next space economy will emerge at the intersection of government, industry and academia.
articles.content: How Nations Can Turn Their Strengths Into Space Leadership | Shelli Brunswick Pick countries on the world map and get breaking news alerts in your browser — free, no app. The next space economy will emerge at the intersection of government, industry and academia. is CEO & Founder of SB Global LLC and an international keynote speaker on tech used for the betterment of humanity. , the session I convened brought together leaders from government, diplomacy, policy, law and industry to explore how international cooperation can expand meaningful participation in space. In Estonia, theThese conversations span different regions, institutions and stages of space development. Yet they point to the same strategic question: How can nations turn what they already do well into a more influential and enduring role in the global space economy? The answer is not to reproduce the world’s largest space programs. Nor is it enough to launch a first satellite, establish an agency or join international discussions. Nations must connect policy with industry, research with commercialization, talent with opportunity and national capabilities with global markets. Start With What A Nation Already Does WellThe space economy operates similarly. A satellite may depend on sensors from one country, software from another, launch services from a third, ground stations elsewhere and data analysis across multiple markets. This structure allows nations to compete through specialization rather than scale. A country with cybersecurity expertise may protect satellites and ground systems. A strong manufacturing sector may produce precision components. Agricultural economies may develop businesses using satellite data. Universities may cultivate expertise in robotics, artificial intelligence, advanced materials, climate science or small-satellite engineering.illustrate different routes to strategic relevance. Slovakia can draw upon its industrial and engineering strengths. Estonia is extending its digital identity into space through software, cybersecurity, resilient infrastructure and commercialization. National advantage often begins outside the space sector. Existing strengths become space capabilities when leaders recognize how they address emerging global needs. The strategic question is not, “What space program should we copy? ” It is, “What can we contribute that others will value? ”Identifying a national strength is only the beginning. Alignment determines whether that potential becomes economic value. Government, industry and academia each control part of the pathway. Governments establish priorities, regulatory confidence and investment conditions. Companies translate technology into products, services, jobs and exports. Universities develop knowledge and talent while producing research that can seed new ventures. A national strategy without commercial pathways may produce ambition without markets. Research without industry connections may remain inside laboratories. Startups without customers, investment or procurement access may struggle to move beyond demonstrations. Workforce programs disconnected from industry demand may prepare people for opportunities that do not yet exist.demonstrates what connected infrastructure can accomplish. It has supported more than 1,800 startups, attracted over €1.25 billion in private investment and produced more than 590 patents between 2020 and 2023. Behind those numbers are relationships linking entrepreneurs with technical expertise, institutional partners, investors, intellectual property guidance and wider markets. Whether a country is developing its first capabilities or seeking greater returns from decades of technical experience, those pathways matter. articles.desc: Company will develop the bedside immune-state readout for a Stanford Medicine-led team awarded $41 million in ARPA-H's CIRCLE critical care program
articles.content: Inflammatix Selected for ARPA-H CIRCLE Program to Bring Precision Immune Medicine to the ICU | FinancialContent Looking for our Business Solutions? Click here: Inflammatix Selected for ARPA-H CIRCLE Program to Bring Precision Immune Medicine to the ICU ⓘ This article is third-party content and does not represent the views of this site. We make no guarantees regarding its accuracy or completeness. Inflammatix, Inc., a precision diagnostics company focused on measurement of the host immune response, today announced its selection as the commercialization collaborator and bedside platform developer for a Stanford Medicine-led team awarded $41 million by the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H). The award is part of ARPA-H's Critical Illness Immunological Reprogramming and Control Point Learning Engine (CIRCLE) program, which aims to reimagine how critically ill patients are cared for in intensive care units. Under the award, Inflammatix will develop and commercialize the bedside immune-state readout that anchors the program: an investigational, rapid, whole-blood test that quantifies each patient's Hi-DEF immune state at the point of care and can be repeated as often as clinical management demands. Paired with a mechanistic digital twin built by the Stanford Medicine team, led by Purvesh Khatri, PhD, Professor of Medicine, the readout is designed to identify each patient's immune subtype and guide selection of the most appropriate immunomodulatory therapy in real time. Roughly 4.6 million Americans are admitted to intensive care units each year, and as many as 30 percent die in the hospital. Sepsis alone accounts for at least 350,000 U.S. deaths annually - more than breast cancer, prostate cancer, and opioid overdoses combined. Survivors frequently leave the hospital with post-ICU syndrome, a long-term condition that can include cognitive impairment, physical debility, and lasting emotional trauma. Despite decades of clinical trials, there is no FDA-approved therapy that targets the dysregulated host immune response driving most of this mortality. Promising drugs help some patients and hurt others, and the averages come out flat. A precision-medicine playbook, borrowed from oncology In the 1970s, breast cancer was largely treated as one disease. The first molecular subtyping came with estrogen and progesterone receptor status; in the 1990s, HER2 added a second axis; in the 2000s, Oncotype DX and other multi-gene assays brought genomic precision to treatment decisions. Today, breast cancer is not treated as one disease but as a dozen, each with tailored therapies - and survival has improved accordingly. Just as importantly, that precision gave drug developers the tools to design therapies for the patients most likely to benefit, fueling an explosion of targeted drugs that would not have been possible in a world of syndrome-based enrollment. Critical illness has yet to make that shift. Patients in the ICU are still classified by presenting syndrome (what put them there) rather than by the underlying immune biology that predicts their trajectory and their response to therapy. CIRCLE is designed to change that by combining continuous bedside measurement of the immune state, mechanistic digital twins that model how each patient will respond, and prospective testing of immunomodulatory interventions matched to biology rather than to syndrome. "The lesson of the last fifty years of oncology is simple: once you can measure molecular subtypes reliably at the bedside, you unlock a generation of therapies designed for the patients they will actually help," said Tim Sweeney, M.D., Ph.D., President and Chief Executive Officer of Inflammatix. "Patients in the ICU deserve that same future, and we intend to help create it. CIRCLE is one of the boldest bets in federal science on getting there, and we are proud to be building the bedside platform that makes it possible." articles.content: Denials of clinical laboratory, molecular diagnostic, and genomics claims rose to 11.2% in 2025 from 8.0% the year before, a 40% jump that erased two years of improvement, according to the recently released 2026 Payor Denial Impact Report from XiFin, Inc., a leader in AI-enabled revenue cycle management (RCM). The report is based on an analysis of more than 30 million claims processed through XiFin’s Empower RCM solution, which serves 11 of the 15 largest laboratories in the United States. 1
